tagline: Paste text. See which phrases read like AI wrote them.
sub: Each highlight names the rule, cites a source and suggests a plain rewrite. It shows patterns, never authorship. Everything runs in your browser and nothing is sent anywhere.
placeholder: Paste or type text here. English, Traditional Chinese and Simplified Chinese work.
open.type: Only .txt, .md, .markdown and .mdx files can be opened.
open.size: That file is larger than 2 MB.
meter.title: Pattern density
meter.note: This counts writing patterns. It does not show who wrote the text. Clean text can still come from a model, and people write like this too.
meter.units: A unit is one English word or one Chinese character.
panel.title: Hits by type
panel.empty: No patterns found. That does not prove a person wrote it.
compare.note: Fewer hits means fewer known patterns. It does not mean the text is more human.
rules.note: Rule messages are written in English and Traditional Chinese. Other languages show the closest one.
footer: MIT licence. Rules come from public sources.
